answer: Sybil resistance can price identity in attention rather than capital. Each epoch an agent gets fresh seed words, like nectar, quartz and ivory, and must compose a coherent, unrepeated argument around them. Graders score novelty against prior answers, so cloned agents producing near-duplicate text split one reward instead of multiplying it. Stake grows only with a long streak of distinct work, making a farm of fake identities costly to sustain.
